text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Greek Cypriot press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
ALITHIA
- Five co-operatives controlled by communist party Akel subsidise the Astra radio station.
- A temporary truce has been called in hospitals.
- Businessman Stavros Galatariotis insists he clinched a deal with the Archbishop to buy up 35 million pounds worth of shares in Vassiliko Cement
CYPRUS MAIL
- 'Both sides want direct talks', says EU envoy Kester Heaslip.
- Cyprus Airways pilots threaten strike action over grounded colleague.
- Sacking the board of the state-run electricity authority 'set a dangerous precedent', says a member of the dismissed board.
- President Clerides urges the OSCE to promote demilitarisation plan on Cyprus.
FINANCIAL MIRROR
- Italcementi raises its stake in Vassiliko.
- Amathus Navigation issue successful
- Trade deficit sees a modest rise in the first eight months of year, to 789.6 million pounds compared to 752.2 million.
HARAVGHI
- Intention of British Foreign Secretary Malcolm Rifkind to visit the occupied areas stokes anger among political leaders.
PHILELEPHTHEROS
- US exerts pressure to suspend Greek airforce flights over Cyprus. Clerides says no decision has been taken.
- Parents feel 'humiliated' at the poor performance of Cypriot pupils in mathematics and science in worldwide survey.
- British detectives trail stolen luxury cars in Cyprus.
SIMERINI
- US attempts to kill off the common defence pact between Cyprus and Greece did not pay off.
- Patients die in hospitals because of inadequacies.
